newly_refused.reason: the reading was refused because the request or reading claims a delay or a speed-up (the request says "When planning escalates the planner to planner_revision_effort (xhigh) on a revision round, scale th", which holds the phrase "cut" and a duration figure) but it has no `Timeline:` assumption; the claimed figure was not checked against the real stage order and durations. The stages of a job run in this order (as `StageMinutes::named` lists them): reading, planning, producer, checks, verifier, landing and rebuild. `athena status` prints the median minutes of each per landed job; a reader with no records takes the durations from the request, or from the timeouts and poll intervals in the code it reads. Add an assumption that starts `Timeline:`, names the crates/ path that runs the stages, lists each stage in order with its duration and whether it is measured, recorded or an estimate, and names the stage where the claimed delay sits. Say whether the request's own figure matches those durations, or label it an `unchecked estimate`; a stage the request names that the code does not run in that order is the usual error, for example: "Timeline: crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs runs reading 3 min (recorded), then planning 9 min (recorded), then producer 14 min (recorded), then checks 6 min (recorded), then verifier 8 min (estimate); the claimed 12 minute delay sits in checks". Plan the change around the stage where the time is spent, not around the figure as the request gave it
